extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting entries to the Archive of Formal Proofs (Isabelle/AFP contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting an Archive of Formal Proofs (AFP) entry written in Isabelle/Isar, including style rules, repository/session layout, build requirements, and update/maintenance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Isabelle style rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission must follow the following Isabelle style rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the umbrella requirement; additional (non-mandatory) Isabelle proof style guidance is linked from the page and may be followed but the listed rules below are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: No use of 'sorry' or 'back'
rubrics_metrics.description: No use of the commands sorry or back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must contain complete proofs; use of sorry (admitting proofs) or back is forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Isabelle-generated names in instantiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Instantiations must not use Isabelle-generated names such as xa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Isar, the subgoal command or rename_tac to avoid Isabelle-generated names.

rubrics_metrics.name: No use of 'sledgehammer' or 'smt_oracle'
rubrics_metrics.description: No use of the commands sledgehammer or smt_oracle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These automated-oracle commands are not permitted in AFP submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: nitpick/quickcheck/nunchaku calls must include 'expect'
rubrics_metrics.description: If your theories contain calls to nitpick, quickcheck, or nunchaku those calls must include the expect parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively the expect parameter may be set globally, e.g. via nitpick_params.

rubrics_metrics.name: apply scripts indentation by subgoal
rubrics_metrics.description: apply scripts should be indented by subgoal as in the Isabelle distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an apply command is applied to a state with n+1 subgoals, it must be indented by n spaces relative to the first apply in the sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only named lemmas should carry attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Only named lemmas should carry attributes such as [simp].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous or local lemmas should avoid carrying global attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isabelle linter will check for violations and anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission process employs the Isabelle linter that checks for most violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The linter will also warn about other anti-patterns; check the end of your build log for such warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for structured Isar proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: We prefer structured Isar proofs over apply style, but do not mandate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to use Isar for readability and maintainability, though apply-style proofs are allowed if they conform to other style rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment long proof steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are proof steps that take significant time, i.e. longer than roughly 1 min, please add a short comment to that step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps maintainers and reviewers know what to expect during builds.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROOT file and session naming
rubrics_metrics.description: The entry must contain a ROOT file with one session that has the name of the entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They strongly encourage precisely one session per entry (exceptions possible). All sessions must be in chapter AFP, and all theory files of the submission must be contained in at least one session. See the example ROOT file in the Example submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission must build on current Isabelle/AFP and produce PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission should run in the current Isabelle/AFP release and produce a PDF document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To test this, run: isabelle build -v -o browser_info -o "document=pdf" -o "document_variants=document:outline=/proof,/ML" -D <entry dir>. Submissions that do not build on the current release are problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite all sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The entry should cite all sources that the theories are based on, for example textbooks or research articles containing informal versions of the proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations should appear in the submission (e.g., in the root.tex) so the provenance of results is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Session timeouts must be divisible by 300 seconds
rubrics_metrics.description: All sessions must have a timeout after which they are assumed to be in a non-terminating state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeouts may be no finer than five-minute increments; i.e., must be divisible by 300.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract required for website; MathJax rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must contain an abstract to be displayed on the web site – usually the same as the abstract of your proof document in the root.tex file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can use MathJax formulae in this web site abstract, either inline ($a+b$ or \(a+b\)) or display ($$a+b$$ or \[a+b\]). MathJax in the title of an entry is not allowed. Other occurrences of these characters must be escaped (e.g. \$ or \()). See MathJax documentation for supported LaTeX features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged to build on other AFP entries
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible and encouraged to build on other archive entries in your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a standardised way to refer to other AFP entries in your theories; use it to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify material suitable for Isabelle distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: It is encouraged to identify parts of your submission as potentially suitable for inclusion in the Isabelle distribution (isabelle/src/HOL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the comment field of the submission form to alert the editors to such material, ideally with a suggestion where it could go (e.g., into List). You may also put it in a separate theory with a descriptive name like More_List.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing and maintenance obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission will be refereed and you will receive notification as soon as possible. If accepted, you must agree to maintain your archive entry or nominate someone else to maintain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Isabelle development team will assist with maintenance, but does not have resources to fully maintain the complete archive; authors are expected to take responsibility for upkeep.

rubrics_metrics.name: If submission depends on development versions, notify editors
rubrics_metrics.description: If your submission can only run on the development version of Isabelle or the AFP, notify the editors after submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need help with Isabelle, use the isabelle-users@cl.cam.ac.uk mailing list and consider subscribing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mercurial development version for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide a new/better version of your AFP entry, you should base your changes on the mercurial development version of your AFP entry and test it against the current Isabelle development version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you would like write access to your entry in the mercurial repository or need assistance, contact the editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating entries: release synchronization and archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: The AFP synchronizes updates with Isabelle releases: the entries visible on the main site work with the most recent stable Isabelle version and do not change; in the background maintainers evolve entries to the current Isabelle development version; when a new Isabelle version is released, the development version is frozen and becomes the main version, and older versions are archived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can contribute to the development version (Heptapod mercurial repo or tar.gz on download page); archival copies of older versions remain accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record significant changes with 'extra-history' metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant changes of an entry should be recorded in the metadata of the entry using the keyword 'extra-history'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should result in the web page showing the extra-history information; see linked example for formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity expectation for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Updating an entry should be mostly monotone: you add new material, but you do not modify existing material in a major way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally entries that others build on should not be affected. If you intend major non-monotone changes, you will need to submit a completely new entry (with a description of how it relates to the old one). Major monotone changes (e.g., adding a new concept rather than more results on existing concepts) may also call for a new entry depending on organization; liaise with other affected authors as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact channels and support
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have questions regarding your submission, email afp-submit@in.tum.de. For general Isabelle help, use the isabelle-users@cl.cam.ac.uk mailing list and consider subscribing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also use the submission form and the editors for assistance; mention if submission relies on development versions.
